f3_program: observe(at("company.cash_flows.investing_activities.net_cash", "2018"), -114, "million_currency", cell("Net cash provided by (used in) investing activities", "December 28, 2018"))
observe(at("company.cash_flows.investing_activities.net_cash", "2017"), -71, "million_currency", cell("Net cash provided by (used in) investing activities", "December 29, 2017"))
query("difference", at("company.cash_flows.investing_activities.net_cash", "2017"), at("company.cash_flows.investing_activities.net_cash", "2018"))
assumptions: Accounting parentheses denote negative cash-flow values, and the table's scale is millions of currency.

f3_program: collection("cyrus.family.other_members", "person", "cyrus.family", source("his entire family of 6 other people"))
observe(at("cyrus.mosquito_bites.arms_and_legs.count", "current"), 14, "count", source("Cyrus counted 14 mosquito bites on his arms and legs"))
observe(at("cyrus.mosquito_bites.body.count", "current"), 10, "count", source("He later counted another 10 on his body"))

sum_relation(at("cyrus.mosquito_bites.total_count", "current"), at("cyrus.mosquito_bites.arms_and_legs.count", "current"), at("cyrus.mosquito_bites.body.count", "current"), source("Cyrus counted 14 mosquito bites on his arms and legs. He later counted another 10 on his body"))
observe(at("cyrus.family.other_members.count", "current"), 6, "count", source("family of 6 other people"))

fraction_of(at("cyrus.family.other_members.mosquito_bites.total_count", "current"), at("cyrus.mosquito_bites.total_count", "current"), 1, 2, source("his entire family of 6 other people only got a total of half the number of bites that Cyrus got"))

quotient_relation(at("cyrus.family.other_member.mosquito_bites.count", "current"), at("cyrus.family.other_members.mosquito_bites.total_count", "current"), at("cyrus.family.other_members.count", "current"), source("they all have an equal number of bites"))
query("value", at("cyrus.family.other_member.mosquito_bites.count", "current"))
assumptions: The later 10 bites are an additional, non-overlapping component of Cyrus's total.
Equal bite counts mean the six other family members share their collective total equally.

f3_program: observe(at("oliver.laundry_shop.charge_rate", "current"), 2, "currency_per_kilogram", source("he charges $2 per kilo of laundry"))
rate_relation("oliver.laundry_shop.earnings", at("oliver.laundry_shop.charge_rate", "current"), "oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_washed", source("he charges $2 per kilo of laundry"))
observe(at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_washed", "two_days_ago"), 5, "kilogram", source("Two days ago, his shop washed a total of 5 kilos of laundries"))

offset(at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_washed", "yesterday"), at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_washed", "two_days_ago"), 5, "kilogram", source("Yesterday, it washed five kilos of laundries more than the previous day"))
multiple(at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_washed", "today"), at("oliver.laundry_shop.laundry_washed", "yesterday"), 2, source("Today, it washed twice the number of kilos than yesterday"))
query("value", at("oliver.laundry_shop.earnings", "three_days"))
assumptions: The three-day period comprises two days ago, yesterday, and today.
The dollar-denominated charge is represented with the generic currency unit rather than an unstated national denomination.

f3_program: collection("martin.party.invited_people", "person", "martin.party", source("he invited many of his colleagues"))
observe(at("martin.party.invited_people.hometown.count", "current"), 5, "count", source("He invited 5 people from his hometown"))

multiple(at("martin.party.invited_people.school.count", "current"), at("martin.party.invited_people.hometown.count", "current"), 2, source("He invited 5 people from his hometown and twice as many people from his school"))

sum_relation(at("martin.party.invited_people.sports_club.count", "current"), at("martin.party.invited_people.hometown.count", "current"), at("martin.party.invited_people.school.count", "current"), source("as many people from his sports club as the sum of people invited from his hometown and his school"))

sum_relation(at("martin.party.invited_people.previously_mentioned.count", "current"), at("martin.party.invited_people.hometown.count", "current"), at("martin.party.invited_people.school.count", "current"), at("martin.party.invited_people.sports_club.count", "current"), source("He invited 5 people from his hometown and twice as many people from his school. Martin invited also as many people from his sports club as the sum of people invited from his hometown and his school"))

percent_of(at("martin.party.invited_people.remaining.count", "current"), at("martin.party.invited_people.previously_mentioned.count", "current"), 20, source("The remaining invitations represent 20% of the total previously mentioned"))

sum_relation(at("martin.party.invited_people.count", "current"), at("martin.party.invited_people.previously_mentioned.count", "current"), at("martin.party.invited_people.remaining.count", "current"), source("The remaining invitations represent 20% of the total previously mentioned"))
query("value", at("martin.party.invited_people.count", "current"))
assumptions: The previously mentioned total comprises the hometown, school, and sports-club invitees.
Each remaining invitation denotes one additional person who could potentially attend.

f3_program: collection("kelly.art_project.supplies", "supply", "kelly.art_project", source("Kelly needs school supplies to teach her class for an art project"))
observe(at("kelly.art_project.students.count", "current"), 8, "count", source("She has 8 students"))
observe(at("kelly.art_project.construction_paper_per_student", "current"), 3, "piece_per_student", source("3 pieces of construction paper each"))

product_relation(at("kelly.art_project.required_supplies.construction_paper.count", "current"), at("kelly.art_project.students.count", "current"), at("kelly.art_project.construction_paper_per_student", "current"), source("She has 8 students and they will need 3 pieces of construction paper each"))
observe(at("kelly.art_project.required_supplies.glue_bottles.count", "current"), 6, "count", source("she needs to buy 6 bottles of glue"))

sum_relation(at("kelly.art_project.required_supplies.count", "current"), at("kelly.art_project.required_supplies.construction_paper.count", "current"), at("kelly.art_project.required_supplies.glue_bottles.count", "current"), source("they will need 3 pieces of construction paper each. In addition to the construction paper, she needs to buy 6 bottles of glue"))
add("initial_supply_purchase", "kelly", at("kelly.art_project.supplies.count", "current"), at("kelly.art_project.required_supplies.count", "current"), source("After Kelly purchases these supplies"))

remove("storm_drain_drop", "kelly", at("kelly.art_project.supplies.count", "current"), fraction(event_field("initial_supply_purchase", "quantity"), 1, 2), source("she dropped half of them down a storm drain"))
add("replacement_construction_paper_purchase", "kelly", at("kelly.art_project.supplies.count", "current"), 5, source("buy 5 more pieces of construction paper"))
query("remaining_count", "kelly.art_project.supplies", "current")
assumptions: “These supplies” and “them” refer collectively to the required construction paper and glue Kelly purchased.
Paper pieces and glue bottles are counted as individual supplies, as implied by the question.
